name: Off-Road Vehicle
description: A vehicle not registered for the street, used for recreation on nonhighway roads, trails or other natural terrain, motorcycles included; an electric dirt bike like a Sur-Ron or Talaria ridden off-road is one. Defined by Revised Code of Washington §46.04.365 and regulated by chapter 46.09 RCW.

restrictions.rule: Not registered for street use, and used recreationally on nonhighway roads, trails or natural terrain; no limit on motor power or speed
Needs an ORV registration and decal from the Department of Licensing, except on agricultural or timber land the owner or operator's employer controls
Every rider must wear a fastened motorcycle helmet on a nonhighway road, except an operator on their own land
Needs adequate brakes, and a headlight and taillight from dusk to dawn on land the rider doesn't own
Allowed on a nonhighway road, and parking areas serving ORV areas, only where the managing authority allows ORVs
Allowed on a street, road or highway only where a city under 3,000 people or a county designates it by ordinance; there it's exempt from street registration and equipment rules

Not allowed on trails or roads restricted to pedestrian or animal travel, on road shoulders or medians, in ways that damage soil or vegetation, or on a private nonhighway road the owner hasn't opened to ORVs
Cities, counties and state agencies may regulate it on land and roads they control, but no less strictly than state law
